Subject: Reliability & SLO follow-up (Redwood vs Hyperscaler)

Hi Sophie — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps focused on reliability/SLOs and competitive comparisons against hyperscaler endpoints.

Call recap (short):
- Primary goal: validate Redwood’s reliability and failover behavior for Acme’s low-latency inference use case (real-time inference, 95th latency target ~120ms).
- Current baseline: Acme running models on AWS SageMaker realtime endpoints, multi-AZ, limited cross-region failover.
- Key concerns: sustained high QPS, throttling patterns (429s), error budget tolerance, cross-region failover behavior, and deterministic fallback in partial outage.

Proposed PoC/tests (we can narrow):
1) Sustained throughput test: 1k qps sustained over 72 hours (profile steady + peak bursts) to validate error-rate and 99.95% uptime target.
2) Throttle/failure injection: deliberate rate-limit and partial node outages to observe 429/5xx surface area and automatic retries/fallbacks.
3) Cross-region failover: simulate region loss and measure failover time and impact on latency/throughput.
4) Comparison run: parallel runs against your current SageMaker setup and a standard hyperscaler-managed endpoint (we can use Vertex or AWS) on identical traffic patterns.

Deliverables we’ll provide: SLO matrix (attached), runbook with test commands, results CSV with latency/error distributions, and recommended config for production (batching/routing/caching settings).

Ask from Acme: can you confirm target test window (we suggested 2026-03-08 to 2026-03-10), peak qps target (if different from 1k), and whether you want us to coordinate a hyperscaler comparison (which provider)?

Attachments: slo-matrix.xlsx (SLO targets & metrics), runbook-failover-testing.pdf

Next steps:
- You: confirm test window and hyperscaler to compare vs (AWS/GCP).
- Us: schedule kickoff, prep test infra and share baseline benchmark link.

Thanks — Ben

Subject: Re: Reliability & SLO follow-up (Redwood vs Hyperscaler)

Sophie — great, thanks for the detail. Short answers here and attached the test artifacts + benchmark CSV from a recent internal run.

Failure modes & automatic fallback (summary):
- Node-level failure: requests routed to healthy nodes in the same region; request-level retry with exponential backoff (max 3 attempts) plus automatic spillover to alternative model shard if cache warm. We keep telemetry for retries to avoid hidden cost/regressions.
- AZ failure: transparent routing to remaining AZs in region with slight latency uplift; Redis-based KV cache replicated across AZs for prefix caching where feasible.
- Region-level failure: policy-driven routing — if a region crosses an error-rate threshold or health probe fails, we route to secondary region(s) (same model family or quantized variant). Failover time typically <30s for control-plane-triggered route switch; in-canary tests we've observed median ~12s with no data loss.
- Rate limits/throttling: per-api-key token-bucket limits with a configurable burst window + steady-state QPS. For bursts we allow short-term token depletion (burst window) and then surface 429s with Retry-After. Our SDKs implement recommended retry/backoff patterns automatically; we also offer queued async ingestion patterns for high sustained loads.

SLOs we operate against (what we propose for PoC):
- Uptime target: 99.95% (monthly), with an error budget policy and automated rollback triggers for non-progressive degradations.
- 95th latency: dependent on model/config; for production real-time targets we advise a combination of warm KV cache + instance sizing to meet 95p requirements.
- Error budget handling: when error budget consumption exceeds the rolling threshold, routing policy will (a) reduce burst windows, (b) move traffic to lower-cost/compatible model variant, and (c) trigger on-call paging and automatic canary rollback.

Test plan (concrete):
- Kickoff: 2026-03-08 09:00 PT.
- Day 0: baseline runs (100 qps, 1k qps steady, 1.6k 15-min spikes) against Redwood + your SageMaker baseline + Vertex.
- Day 1: failure injection (node kill, AZ degrade).
- Day 2: cross-region failover + long-sustained 72h soak if you want deeper coverage.

Files attached: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-runs-20260303.csv (sample run results), slo-matrix.xlsx, runbook-failover-testing.pdf.

Do you have any constraints on peering or credentials? If not, we can run the hyperscaler comparison from our controlled harness (we’ll share the scripts/traffic profile) so you don’t need to provision anything beyond short-lived test creds.

If that looks good, I’ll schedule the kickoff and loop in our infra team to prepare canary routing configs.

— Ben
